items.title: Pocketpair (Palworld) shares photos from its free day because of GTA VI
items.summary: As most people know, Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launched today, November 19, 2026. It was a long (or very short) night for some, though not for everyone.…
items.content:
As most people know, Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launched today, November 19, 2026. It was a long (or very short) night for some, though not for everyone.

In fact, Pocketpair, the studio behind Palworld , organized a celebration to mark the release of Rockstar’s famous title. The offices were transformed into a full-fledged party venue with decorations, a large spread of food, and TVs and consoles set up to try out GTA VI .

Today is Pocketpair’s GTA 6 holiday! 🎮 We’re celebrating with an office launch party for those who want to come in, with sushi, drinks, and GTA 6! 🍣 We’ve also set up a bunch of consoles in the break room so anyone can play whenever they want! pic.twitter.com/7AtgiFy1fa

items.title: Palworld developer Pocketpair gives employees a five-day 'business trip' to Vice City for GTA 6's launch
items.summary: Palworld developer Pocketpair gives staff November 19-23 off to play GTA 6, a five-day break that includes a weekend and uses three days of leave.
items.content:
Palworld developer Pocketpair gives staff November 19-23 off to play GTA 6, a five-day break that includes a weekend and uses three days of leave.

VIEW GALLERY - 2 Grand Theft Auto 6 imagery accompanies Pocketpair's announcement that employees who want to play at launch can take November 19–23 off. 1 Hamid Murtaza Tech Reporter Published Nov 15, 2026 7:15 AM CST 1 minute & 15 seconds read time What you need to know Pocketpair gave employees planning to play GTA 6 time off from November 19 - 23, framing it as a Vice City business trip. The five-day span includes a weekend, so it uses three leave days. Palworld and Craftopia updates will continue as scheduled.

As an Amazon Associate, we earn from qualifying purchases. TweakTown may also earn commissions from Walmart and other affiliate partners at no extra cost to you.

With GTA 6 set to launch on November 19, offices everywhere are likely bracing for a wave of time-off requests. Pocketpair, the indie studio behind Palworld, got ahead of the curve by granting employees a five-day vacation to play the game. In a tweet on November 12, the studio jokingly announced that all staff had been "granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches."

Go ad-free with Supporter See plans and prices

In a memo to staff, Pocketpair leaned into the anticipation around the release. "On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," the company wrote. "At Pocketpair, we believe such a historic occasion deserves our full attention."

From November 19 to November 23, employees who intend to play GTA 6 will be excused from their regular duties and encouraged to take that business trip to Vice City. Since the stretch includes a weekend, it technically works out to three days of leave rather than five, but who's counting? The studio also noted that updates for Palworld and Craftopia will continue as scheduled, so nobody needs to reach for the pitchforks.

CEO Takuro Mizobe joined in on the fun too, saying he'll be playing, too. "Of course, I'll be taking a break for a while to play GTA 6 too!"

Pocketpair isn't the only company handing out time off. Logitech announced Logi Game Day on November 19, giving its 7,000 employees a day off to play games, including GTA 6. Robin Piispanen, general manager of Logitech G, said staff are free to play whatever they like.

2 Logitech’s Game Day graphic promotes time off to play; the company announced that its 7,000 employees would have November 19 off, coinciding with GTA 6’s planned launch. VIEW GALLERY - 2 IMAGES The celebration goes well beyond the tech world, too. California-based automotive parts manufacturer Burger Motorsports said in a social media statement that it would observe a "temporary company-wide operational pause" on launch day. Canadian truck maker Edison Motors said it would give its employees a four-day weekend starting November 19.

items.title: Pocketpair Gives Staff 5 Days Off for GTA VI [2026]
items.summary: Pocketpair GTA VI leave gives eligible staff five days off, Nov. 19 to 23. See what the memo says, what is unconfirmed, and what it means.
items.content:
Image: Pocketpair Pocketpair, the studio behind Palworld, has told its staff to treat the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI as a business trip. The company granted five days of special leave covering November 19 to 23, 2026, according to the Palworld official account and coverage from IGN, PC Gamer and Push Square. The Pocketpair GTA VI leave starts on the game’s launch day and runs through the following Monday.

Pocketpair GTA VI Leave: What the Studio Announced The Five-Day Calendar: Three Workdays and a Weekend Reading the Palworld Account’s Wording The post: a business trip, not a vacation The memo: a holiday with a condition Who Qualifies: The Intent-to-Play Condition The Riot Claim: What the Record Does Not Say Palworld and Craftopia Updates Stay on Schedule Why a Studio Can Afford This Joke The GTA VI Launch Run-Up in Dates Launch Week and the Workplace: Four Signals Compared Market and Industry Impact Five Predictions for the Launch Window What to Watch Between Now and Nov. 23 FAQ: Pocketpair’s GTA VI Leave Related Coverage The official post described the time off as a special leave to attend to “an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.” That joke has a real condition attached. Reports say the leave applies to employees who intend to play the game, and the memo excuses them from their regular duties. For readers tracking the final stretch before release, our GTA 6 launch-week rundown covers the confirmed date, platforms and prices.

This analysis separates what Pocketpair actually said from what the internet added on top. It walks through the calendar, the wording, the eligibility rule, the Palworld and Craftopia update schedule, and the wider workplace picture around Rockstar’s biggest release. It also flags one claim in circulating headlines, that staff might riot without the break, which the official material does not contain.

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

The announcement came through the Palworld official account on X, according to PC Gamer, and it arrived with a memo attached. GTA Boom reported that the memo sat on company letterhead and carried a six-star wanted-level graphic in the corner, a nod to Rockstar’s own series imagery. GTA Boom described the document as a special company holiday announcement.

Outlets agree on the core facts. The leave lasts five days. It begins November 19, the scheduled worldwide launch date for Grand Theft Auto VI, and ends November 23. Push Square described it as a special holiday for Palworld developer employees, and Inven Global covered the announcement from the angle of workers at other companies. VGTimes, TBreak and ConsolePCGaming ran the same basic story the same day.

The memo’s own wording is the cleanest guide to intent. Eligible employees would be “excused from their regular duties” for the period, and the company encouraged them to treat the time as a trip to Vice City, the fictional setting of the game. Nothing in the quoted text sets out pay terms, a sign-up process, a rota, or a cap on how many people can take the leave at once. Those details may exist internally, but they are not in the public record.

The tone matters as much as the policy. Pocketpair chose to joke about its own productivity rather than pretend the launch would pass unnoticed. A studio with two games in active update cycles gets attention for that kind of move. The memo works as a recruiting poster, a fan wink and an HR notice in one document.

The dates fall in an unusual place. November 19, 2026, is a Thursday and November 23 is a Monday. The Pocketpair GTA VI leave therefore spans a full weekend, and on a standard Monday-to-Friday schedule it covers three normal workdays: Thursday, Friday and Monday. Reports on the announcement made the same observation.

That math shrinks the cost of the gesture. Three lost workdays out of a month is a modest price for a company that wants goodwill and a viral headline. It also shows the joke was well timed. Launching on a Thursday gives players a long weekend with a single extra day on each side.

One caveat applies. The reports describe a standard week, but they do not describe Pocketpair’s internal working calendar. If the studio runs different hours or staggers shifts, the real number of working days affected could differ. Treat the three-workday figure as an outside reading of the dates, not a figure Pocketpair published.

The Palworld account never used the word vacation in the quoted line. It called the time an urgent business trip. That framing is the whole joke, and it is a careful one. A trip implies the employees are still on the clock in spirit, which lets the company wave at the idea that playing the biggest game of the year counts as market research.

The Sunlit Isle (405, -483) Pros: Several crude oil nodes, easy to defend during raids Cons: No nearby ore Closest teleport: Sunlit Isle It's not the best spot for ore or stone, but the Sunlit Isle just east of Palworld's starting area makes early game crude oil farming a breeze with six nodes scattered across the land. I like building at the highest point along the island's south side, but there's a cute spot northeast with stone steps leading up to it that works just as well. Even if you intend to go elsewhere for ore farming, this is a great place to build a second base for a steady crude oil supply.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

items.title: v1.0.2: Bug fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released! This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues. ＝＝＝ ▼Crashes and Disconnections ・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released!

This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues.

＝＝＝

▼Crashes and Disconnections

・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where players could crash during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where the game could crash when attempting Japanese text input in fullscreen mode.

▼Multiplayer

・Fixed an issue where, if a player was already in The World Tree area when the host transitioned to The World Tree area, the terrain could fail to display correctly from the host’s perspective.

・Fixed an issue where the Tower Boss “Victor & Shadowbeak” could disappear after using a teleportation attack during battle.

・Fixed an issue in the final boss battle where, if the host defeated the final boss while a guest was waiting to respawn, the guest’s light could fail to display correctly after respawning.

▼Missions

・Fixed an issue in the main mission “The First Islander” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

・Fixed an issue in the sub-mission “Captured Adventurer” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

▼Achievements

・Fixed an issue where the “Predator Hunter” achievement could fail to unlock even after meeting its requirements.

・Fixed an issue where the corresponding achievement could fail to unlock even after obtaining the required Pal Effigies.

・Fixed an issue on Xbox where the icons for two Lifmunk Effigy-related achievements were using outdated versions.

▼Graphics and Display

・Fixed an issue where the eye area of the player model could display incorrectly during cutscenes or certain player actions when using specific face types.

▼Controls

・Added key rebinding for "Attack that enemy!" and "Inventory".

・Fixed an issue where, when carrying over settings from versions earlier than v0.7, changes unrelated to Controls could still be treated as control setting conflicts.

・Fixed an issue where assigning a player action to the middle mouse button could incorrectly be treated as a conflict, preventing the setting from being applied.

・Fixed an issue where the Inventory Shortcut option was not displayed in Controls.

▼UI

・Fixed an issue where the damage number displayed when destroying ore while mining could sometimes appear as 0.

▼Performance Improvements

・Reduced the processing load during gameplay in Sunreach and improved performance.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.
